content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: targeted overtime on both queues at the peak hours, coaching cancelled and callbacks on payments. Predicted 81.7% service level for 08:30-15:15 against the 80% target, at ₹12,900.","why":"Payments is short-staffed (11 agents on the phones against 17 planned) mainly because 8 agents are late due to a bus strike and 1 is off sick. Call volume is close to normal, so this is a staffing problem rather than a demand problem. General is also short (8 absences against a usual 2.4), so it can't lend agents and needs cover of its own. Doing nothing gives 63.0% over the disruption window. The cheaper options only reach 63.2% (P1) and 71.5% (P2). P3 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It lifts payments to 86.6% and general to 75.3%, cuts abandons to 3.5% (from 8.2%), and gives 87.3% for the rest of the day.","trade_offs":["Cost: P3 costs ₹12,900, against ₹300 for P1 and ₹2,652 for P2. Both cheaper plans miss the 80% target by a wide margin.","Other queue: general still sits below target at 75.3%. P4 would lift it to 86.8% (payments 93.8%, 90.8% overall), but at ₹19,212, which is ₹6,312 more.","Risk: P3 clears the target by only 1.7 points and depends on enough agents accepting the overtime offers, especially the 10 payments agents needed for 10:00-12:00."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptance before 10:00 and service level on both queues hourly. If take-up is short or general keeps falling, consider moving to P4's extra general overtime and chat deflection. If the late bus-strike agents start arriving, scale the overtime back."}
